doc.title: James Hunter interviewed by Monk Rowe, Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Musical heroes and record shopping
summary: Hunter names Eddie Cochran, Gene Vincent, Ray Charles, the Five Royales and Clyde McPhatter, and recalls hunting records in Southend-on-Sea.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well when I was a teenager it was I think Eddie Cochran and Gene Vincent I got into. From them into Ray Charles, or that might have been simultaneous. And then I went more sort of underground and discovered the Five Royales and that was, I remember when we worked with Allen Toussaint he was quite what do you call it, impressed that I’d even heard of them because he said that back in the day it was only really ultra-hip black people had heard of the Five Royales. They were a regional phenomenon. They weren’t a world-wide, a nation-wide success, they were a regional act. And a bit of an underground secret, even in their prime.
Were you a guy, when you were young went to the record stores.

Yeah. Browsed through for pretty obscure stuff and that. I remember reading about Clyde McPhatter and deciding, just on the description, that he was my favorite singer. I’d never heard him. But the way this bloke described his voice I thought I’ve got to hear this. And this is about 1980s. You couldn’t find it. They weren’t re-issuing that sort of stuff. And so I went in this little record shop in Southend-on-Sea on my lunch break, because that was Southend-on-Sea in Essex was within our jurisdiction as a signal box maintenance man. So on my lunch break I went off to this little place and they had a box full of, they were reissued singles that you couldn’t find most places. So I got firsthand proof of how good he was.
You know the thing you mentioned, liner notes, were great back then.
Yeah. You had something to read.
Yes you had something to read and, as you said, it might catch your ear through reading it. What do you envision five years from now for yourself and your band?
